paper.title_en: Large-Scale Cosmic-Ray Anisotropy in the TeV Regime: Peak Observables and a Propagation-Model Interpretation
paper.abstract_en: In recent years, cosmic-ray observations have entered a stage of high-precision measurements, but the phases of large-scale anisotropy reported by different experiments differ significantly, partly because the first harmonic cannot fully describe non-dipolar structures. In this work, we process the one-dimensional relative-intensity distributions from ARGO-YBJ, Tibet AS$γ$, and HAWC using a unified procedure, perform multi-harmonic fits, and reconstruct the distributions, with the global maximum of each distribution used to define the peak amplitude $A_{\max}$ and the peak right ascension $α_{\max}$. The results show that, in the common energy range of 11--22~TeV covered by the three experiments, the range of the published first-harmonic phases is $22.6^\circ$, whereas the range of $α_{\max}$ is reduced to $7.5^\circ$; $α_{\max}$ evolves overall from $60^\circ$--$70^\circ$ at the low-energy end to $250^\circ$--$300^\circ$ at the high-energy end, while $A_{\max}$ exhibits a local minimum and $α_{\max}$ changes rapidly in the phase-flip region. At the low-energy end, $α_{\max}$ lies between the right-ascension projections of the direction toward the Geminga supernova remnant and the direction of the local interstellar magnetic field. Accordingly, we construct a spatially dependent propagation model that includes Galactic background sources, a Geminga-related nearby source, and anisotropic diffusion along the direction of the local interstellar magnetic field. Within a unified framework, the model reproduces the energy spectra of P, He, C, O, and Fe, as well as the energy evolution of $A_{\max}$ and $α_{\max}$, providing a self-consistent explanation for the origin of large-scale anisotropy in the TeV to tens-of-TeV energy range.
